paragraphs: highly powerful Mahcndra being thus defeated by Ravana’s son, all the celestials, taking the patriarch BrahmS. before them, went to Lanka. Having obtained RSvana encircled by his sons and brothers the Patriarch, stationed in the welkin, calmly said — “My son, Havana, I have been pleased with thy son in the conflict. Oh ! what wonderful prowess, what strength — equal or greater than thine. Thou. hast, by thy own prowess, conquered the three worlds — thy promise hath borne fruits — I have been pleased with you — both the father and son. O Havana, this thy son is highly powerful and gifted with great strength and he shall be celebrated in the world under the appellation of ‘Indrajit’ or the conqueror of Indra.

And that Rakshasa shall be JiAMA YANA. powerful and irrepressible, by whose help, O king, the celestials have been brought under thy subjection. Do thou therefore, O thou having long arms, release Mahendra, the chastiser of Paka and for setting him free what do thou want from the celestials ?” Thereupon the highly powerful Indrajit — the subduer of enepiies, said : — “If dost thou say so, O god, I pray for immortality.’' Thereat the highly powerful patriarch said to Meghanada — “There is none perfectly immortal on earth amongst created beings — birds, quadrupeds littered by the grand-father — the highly powerful Meghanada said to the eternal lord — ‘“Hear, then, what I want in exchange for releasing Sakra.

May a chariot with horses rise up from fire when I shall offer sacrifices unto it, being desirous of vanquishing my enemies in the conflict. And may I be immortal as long as I shall remain on that car. This is the boon I have resolved upon praying lor. May I meet with ■destruction, O deity, whenever I shall engage in fight without finishing my offerings unto fire. All others, O god, attain to immortality by virtue of devout penances but I shall acquire that by dint of my own prowess.” Whereto the grand-father replied saying “so be it.” Thereupon Meghanada released Indra and the celestials returned to their own abode. In the interval, O Rama, Indra became poorly, divested of his immortal brilliance, stricken with anxiety and pensive.

Beholding him in that plight the grand-father of the deities -said : — “O performer of hundred sacrifices, why didst thou formerly perpetrate that mighty iniquity ? O Chief of the immortals ! G lord !, some creatures were created by me by dint of my understanding — they were all of the same colour, same speech, and same appearance. There was no difference visible in their appearance or marks. Thereupon, with whole-minded-ness, I began to think of these created beings. And I created a female distinct from them. Collecting all those limbs that were most excellent amongst the created, I made a female under the name of Ahalya. Ilal means ugliness — one born from //<z/ is called 1 hat female was known as Ahalya because she had nothing blameable in her. 1 gave her that name.

Having created that female I was thinking, O king of the celestials ! O foremost of the deities !, on whom I should confer her. Being proud of dignity, O Sakra, O lord, O Purandara thou didst regard her ill thy mind as thy spouse. I placed her under the care of the high-souled Gautama and lie rendered her back after many long years. Thereupon considering the patience and accomplished asceticism of Gautama I married her with him. And that virtuous-soulcd, great ascetic enjoyed her company ; and for my thus conferring her upon Gautama all the celestials were disappointed. But being enraged and possessed by lust thou didst repair to the hermitage of the ascetic and sec her rcsplenclant like the flaming fire.

Maddened with lust and ire thou didst ravish her and thou wast seen in that hermitage by the great ascetic. Thou wast then imprecated by him, enraged and gifted with great effulgence saying, ‘O lord of the celestials, thou hast attained to a change of circumstances — for which, O Vasava, thou hast fearlessly ravished my spouse. Thou shalt, therefore, O Sakra, go under the arms of the enemies, in conflict. And this vile desire, O thou having a vicious intellect, which thou hast first created, shall undoubtedly spread in the world of mortals. Whoever shall commit this crime, shall be half responsible for it and the other half shall descend ujjon thee ; and forsooth thy position shall not be permanent.

And whoever shall be the lord of the celestials, shall not have his position secure. This is the curse I give, which I have communicated to thee.’ And having remonstrated with his wife that one of devout penances said to her — ‘O vicious one, let thy beauty be spoiled in the vicinity of the hermitage. 'I'hou art gifted with beauty and youth but thy mind is fickle ; so thou shalt not continue as the single beautiful damsel in the uorld. All creat- /^AJLIVANJ. cd beings shall participate thy beauty ; thy matcliless beauty hari brought about this mischief.’ Thenceforward all created beings were gifted with beauty. Thereupon she propitiated the ascetic Gautama saying, “O twice-born one, I was unwittingly ravished by Indra, assuming thy form.

I have not committed this willingly, O ascetic — so do thou be propitiated with me.” Ahalya having said this, (iautama replied : — “In the race of Ikshwakus, there shall be born a highly effulgent and mighty car-warrior, known in the world as Rama ; for performing the rites of a Brahman, the mighty-armed Vishnu, assuming a human form, shall repair to the forest. Thou shalt be purified when thou shalt behold him,0 fair damsel. He shall be able to purify thee from the iniquity perpetrated. Having treated him as a guest when thou shalt come to me again, thou shalt live with me, 0 thou having a fair countenance.” Having said this that ascetic returned to his hermitage.

And thenceforward the wife, of that ascetic ch.anting the themes of Brahman, engaged in austere penances. Thou hast met with all this in consequence of the imprecation of that ascetic. Therefore, () thou having long arms, do tliQu think of thy past iniquity. For that curse and nothing else, O Vasava, thou hast been brought under the grasp of enemies. Having controlled thy sense.s, do thou soon undertake a sacrifice in honor of Vishnu. Thou shalt be purified by that sacrifice and go to heaven ; and thy son, O lord of celestials, hath not been destroyed in the conflict. He hath Been taken into the ocean by his grand father.” Hearing this and having celelirated the sacrifice in honor of V^ishnu he again went to the region of celestials and reigned there as their king.

I have thus described to thee the strength of Indrajit — what to speak of others he vanquished even Indra — the king of the celestials.” Hearing the words of Agastya, Rama, Lakshmana, Vanaras and R.akshasas all said wonderful it is" ; and Bibhishana, nnIio was by the si'le *.'1 Jeama, serai : ' After a UTTAA\l/OlY/)AJ/. long time, the old recollections have come to my mind.’’ 7'liereujx)n Rama said to Agastya — “All, thou hast said, is true.” And Agastya said “ Rama^ Ravana, the thorn of people, then grew in power, by whom, in the company of his son, Indra, ihe lord of the celestials, was defeated. o £ C T I OiN XXXVI. rp i HF.RF.L'PON having bowed unto Agastya the foremost of ascctic,s, the h.ighly effulgent Rama again surprisingly said : — “ O iirahman, () foremost of twice-born ones, when that cruel Ravana journeyed over the earth, \vas it void of people?

Was there no king, or prince on earth to administer punishment unto him ? Were all the kings then shorn of their strength and prowess? And many kings I (hear) W'cre vanquished and driven out by him with various excellent ■weapons.’ Hearing the vrords of Raghava, the ascetic Agastya, having six sorts of wealth, laugliing said, like unto Brahma, .speaking to Rudra — “ (.) Rama, O lord of earth, traversing the (:;iiili, R.avana arrived at the city of Mahismati, resembling tlu; cii)- o! (In; re'estin.Is, where lived perpetually the (U ity of fire, 'i'here reigned a king named Arjuna, effulgent like lire wRicli was kept j)erpctually in a well covered with Sara. One day tlie ])ighly powerful Arjuna, the king of J'/a ihayas, rej^iared to the river Nerbuda, w'ith his wives to sport.

At the very same day, Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, arrived there- and asked his councillors saying. “Where is /^.IJ/AV.INA. the king Arjuna ? Do ye speedily tell me; lam Ravana, I have come to fight with your king. Do ye, at first, communicate unto him the news of my arrival.” Being thus addressed by Ravana, the learned ministers informed the lord of Rakshasas, of the absence of the king. Hearing of the absence of the king from the citizens Visrasraba’s son came out of the city and reached the Vindliya mountain resembling the Himalayas. He espied the mountain extending over the welkin like unto clouds and rising up as if riving the earth and obstructing the sky. The mountain had a thousand summits and the lions were residing in the caves and hundreds of fountain were falling from it; the mountain was as if laughing aloud and the celestials, Gandharbas, Apsaras and Kinsaras were sporting there with their femviles ; and it appeared (in consequence thereof) like the region of celestials.; and rivers, with waters transparent like crystal, were flowing.

And it therefore appeared like a thousand serpents having trembling tongues. And casting his looks upon Vindhya mountain, resembling the Himalayas and having huge caves^ Ravana, the king of Rakshasas, reached the rivCr Nerbuda, of holy waters and jjoing rapidly to the western ocean. Her waters were being agitated by buffaloes, deer, tigers, lions, bears and elephants distressed by heat. Having covered her, Chakrabakas, Karandavas, swans, water-cocks and Sarasas, maddened, were emitting notes. The charming Nerbuda aiipeared like a beautiful damsel — having blossoming trees for her ornaments, Chakrabakas for her breast, wide spread forest for her waist, the row of swans for Mckhala, filam.ents of flow(n-s for paste, watery foams for white silken cloth, tlic pleasure of descending into water for the pleasure of touch and full-blown lotuses for white eyes.

Having descended from his car and bathed in the waters of Nerbuda, tl.c foremost of streams, n'sembling a fair one, Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, with his co incilfcrs, sat on her coast resided by n\any am ascetic. Delighted at her beauty and having spoken highly of Ncrbutla like unto Ganges he addressed his ministers Suka and Sarana with gestures, saying : — ‘‘Behold, having rendered the earth pale, with his many rays, the sun, emitting parching heat, is in the sky. But seeing me here seated, his rays have becotjie co'ol like those of the moon. At my fear, even the wind is blowing carefully, being cold and fragrant by the touch of the waters of the Nurbnda and removing our toil.

This charming Nerbuda, abounding in crocodiles, fishes and birds, though a natural stream, is standing still like a terrified damsel. Being wounded in conflicts with many a king yottr perso»ns have been j>asted with blood. Therefore like unto Sarvabhauma and other infuriated elephants going down into the water of the Ganges, do ye descend into the water 6f Nerbuda conferrkig auspiciousness and health. Bathing in this stream you shall be cleansed from sins. I shall, also on the coast of this river, like the rays of the autumnal moon, reverentially worship with flowers Mahadeva, holding PinSka in his hands.” Hearing the words of Ravana, Prahasta, Suka, .Sarana, Mahodara, Dhrumakshya and other councillors descended into the waters of Nerbuda. And she was agitated by those elephantlike leading Rakshasas like unto the Ganges by Vamana, Anjana, Padma and other elephants, Thereupon having got up from the waters the highly powerful Rakshasas culled flowers for Ravana’s offerings.

And in a moment the Rakshasas collected, lie.'ips of flowers on the picturesque banks of Nerbuda, ic'sembling the white clouds. Flowers being thus collected, Ravana, the king of Rakshasas descended, into the Nerbuda for bathing like a huge elephant into the Ganges. And having bathed he got up, reciting excellent incantation.s. Thereupon having left off his w'Ct cloth he put on. a white one. And to find out place for worshipping, he, with folded hands, proceeded towards the banks. And the Rakshasas too, like unto so RAMA YANA. many moving mountains, followed him. And wherever Ravana went the golden Siva Linga was brought. Thereupon RSvana placed that upon a heap of sands and began to worship it with various nectar-smelling flowers and sandal. And having finished the worship of Siva, the foremost of deities, having the moon on his crown, the conferrer of boons and the remover of miseries, the night-ranger danced with uplifted hand.s and sang before it.

verses.sa:
ततो रामो महातेजा विस्मयात्पुनरेव हि ।
उवाच प्रणतो वाक्यमगस्त्यमृषिसत्तमम् ॥

भगवन्राक्षसः क्रूरो यदाप्रभृति मेदिनीम् ।
पर्यटत्किं तदा लोकाः शून्या आसन्द्विजोत्तम ॥

राजा वा राजमात्रो वा किं तदा नात्र कश्चन ।
धर्षणं यत्र न प्राप्तो रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः ॥

उताहो हतवीर्यास्ते बभूवुः पृथिवीक्षितः ।
बहिष्कृता वरास्त्रैश्च बहवो निर्जिता नृपाः ॥

राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ह्यगस्त्यो भगवानृषिः ।
उवाच रामं प्रहसन्पितामह इवेश्वरम् ॥

इत्येवं बाधमानस्तु पार्थिवान्पार्थिवर्षभ ।
चचार रावणो राम पृथिवीं पृथिवीपते ॥

ततो माहिष्मतीं नाम पुरीं स्वर्गपुरीप्रभाम् ।
सम्प्राप्तो यत्र सान्निध्यं सदासीद्वसुरेतसः ॥

तुल्य आसीन्नृपस्तस्य प्रभावाद्वसुरेतसः ।
अर्जुनो नाम यत्राग्निः शरकुण्डेशयः सदा ॥

तमेव दिवसं सो ऽथ हैहयाधिपतिर्बली ।
अर्जुनो नर्मदां रन्तुं गतः स्त्रीभिः सहेश्वरः ॥

तमेव दिवसं सो ऽथ रावणस्तत्र आगतः ।
रावणो राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तस्यामात्यानपृच्छत ॥

क्वार्जुनो नृपतिः शीघ्रं सम्यगाख्यातुमर्हथ ।
रावणो ऽहमनुप्राप्तो युद्धेप्सुर्नृवरेण ह ।
ममागमनमप्यग्रे युष्माभिः सन्निवेद्यताम् ॥

इत्येवं रावणेनोक्तास्ते ऽमात्याः सुविपश्चितः ।
अब्रुवन्राक्षसपतिमसान्निध्यं महीपतेः ॥

श्रुत्वा विश्रवसः पुत्रः पौराणामर्जुनं गतम् ।
अपसृत्यागतो विन्ध्यं हिमवत्सन्निभं गिरिम् ॥

स तमभ्रमिवाविष्टमुद्भ्रन्तमिव मेदिनीम् ।
अपश्यद्रावणो विन्ध्यमालिखन्तमिवाम्बरम् ॥

सहस्रशिखरोपेतं सिंहाध्युषितकन्दरम् ।
प्रपातपतितैस्तोयैः साट्टहासमिवाम्बुधिम् ॥

देवदानवगन्धर्वैः साप्सरोगणकिन्नरैः ।
स्वस्त्रीभिः क्रीडमानैश्च स्वर्गभूतं महोच्छ्रयम् ॥

नदीभिः स्यन्दमानाभिः स्फटिकप्रतिमं जलम् ।
फणाभिश्चलजिह्वाभिरनन्तमिव विष्ठितम् ॥

उत्क्रामन्तं दरीवन्तं हिमवत्सन्निभं गिरिम् ।
पश्यमानस्ततो विन्ध्यं रावणो नर्मदां ययौ ॥
चलोपलजलां पुण्यां पश्चिमोदधिगामिनीम् ॥

महिषैः सृमरैः सिंहैः शार्दूलर्क्षगजोत्तमैः ।
उष्णाभितप्तैस्तृषितैः सङ्क्षोभितजलाशयाम् ॥

चक्रवाकैः सकारण्डैः सहंसजलकुक्कुटैः ।
सारसैश्च सदा मत्तैः सुकूजद्भिः समावृताम् ॥

फुल्लद्रुमकृतोत्तंसां चक्रवाकयुगस्तनीम् ।
विस्तीर्णपुलिनश्रोणीं हंसावलिसुमेखलाम् ॥

पुष्परेण्वनुलिप्ताङ्गीं जलफेनामलांशुकाम् ।
जलावगाहसंस्पर्शां फुल्लोत्पलशुभेक्षणाम् ।
पुष्पकादवरुह्याशु नर्मदां सरितां वराम् ॥

इष्टामिव वरां नारीमवगाह्य दशाननः ।
स तस्याः पुलिने रम्ये नानामुनिनिषेविते ॥

उपोपविष्टैः सचिवैः सार्धं राक्षसपुङ्गवः ।
प्रख्याय नर्मदां सो ऽथ गङ्गेयमिति रावणः ॥

नर्मदादर्शजं हर्षमाप्तवान् राक्षसाधिपः ।
उवाच सचिवांस्तत्र सलीलं शुकसारणौ ॥

एष रश्मिसहस्रेण जगत्कृत्वैव काञ्चनम् ।
तीक्ष्णतापकरः सूर्यो नभसो ऽर्धं समाश्रितः ॥
मामासीनं विदित्वैव चन्द्रायति दिवाकरः ॥

नर्मदाजलशीतश्च सुगन्धिः श्रमनाशनः ।
मद्भयादनिलो ऽप्यत्र वात्येष सुसमाहितः ॥

इयं वापि सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा नर्मदा नर्मवर्धिनी ।
नक्रमीनविहङ्गोर्मिः सभयेवाङ्गना स्थिता ॥

तद्भवन्तः क्षताः शस्त्रैर्नृपैरिन्द्रसमैर्युधि ।
चन्दनस्य रसेनेव रुधिरेण समुक्षिताः ॥

ते यूयमवगाहध्वं नर्मदां शर्मदां शुभाम् ।
महापद्ममुखा मत्ता गङ्गामिव गहागजाः ।
अस्यां स्नात्वा महानद्यां पाप्मानं विप्रमोक्ष्यथ ॥

अहमप्यद्य पुलिने शरदिन्दुसमप्रभे ।
पुष्पोपहारं शनकैः करिष्यामि कपर्दिनः ॥

रावणेनैवमुक्तास्तु प्रहस्तशुकसारणाः ।
समहोदरधूम्राक्षा नर्मदां विजगाहिरे ॥

राक्षसेन्द्रगजैस्तैस्तु क्षोभिता नर्मदा नदी ।
वामनाञ्जनपद्माद्यैर्गङ्गा इव महागजैः ॥

ततस्ते राक्षसाः स्नात्वा नर्मदायां महाबलाः ।
उत्तीर्य पुष्पाण्याजह्रुर्बल्यर्थं रावणस्य तु ॥

नर्मदापुलिने हृद्ये शुभ्राभ्रसदृशप्रभे ।
राक्षसैस्तु मुहूर्तेन कृतः पुष्पमयो गिरिः ॥

पुष्पेषूपहृतेष्वेवं रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः ।
अवतीर्णो नदीं स्नातुं गङ्गामिव महागजः ॥

तत्र स्नात्वा च विधिवज्जप्त्वा जप्यमनुत्तमम् ।
नर्मदासलिलात्तस्मादुत्ततार स रावणः ॥

ततः क्लिन्नाम्बरं त्यक्त्वा शुक्लवस्त्रसमावृतम् ।
रावणं प्राञ्जलिं यान्तमन्वयुः सर्वराक्षसाः ॥

तद्गतीवशमापन्ना मूर्तिमन्त इवाचलाः ।
यत्र यत्र च याति स्म रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः ।
जाम्बूनदमयं लिङ्गं तत्र तत्र स्म नीयते ॥

वालुकावेदिमध्ये तु तल्लिङ्गं स्थाप्य रावणः ।
अर्चयामास गन्धैश्च पुष्पैश्चामृतगन्धिभिः ॥

ततः सतामार्तिहरं परं वरं वरप्रदं चन्द्रमयूखभूषणम् ।
समर्चयित्वा स निशाचरो जगौ प्रसार्य हस्तान्प्रणनर्त चाग्रतः ॥
